title: Colgan 3407: first officer's icing confession and pitch-hold hedge
date: 2009-02-12 UTC (CVR 22:11:42.5 to 22:12:37.6, about five minutes before the stall)
setting: Cockpit voice recorder transcript (Appendix B of NTSB AAR-10-01), Bombardier Q400, descending toward Buffalo in icing conditions. HOT = cockpit area/hot mic; radio calls interleaved in original time order. Time stamps and page-break headers removed.
public_domain_basis: NTSB accident report (US Government work, 17 U.S.C. 105).

turns.speaker: Captain (cockpit)
turns.text: no but uh out of that six and a quarter two hundred fifty hours was uh part one twenty one turbine. multi engine turbine.

turns.speaker: First Officer (cockpit)
turns.text: no but all these guys are complaining they're saying you know how we were supposed to upgrade by now and they're complaining I'm thinking you know what? I really wouldn't mind going through a a winter in the northeast before I have to upgrade to captain.

turns.speaker: First Officer (cockpit)
turns.text: I've never seen icing conditions. I've never deiced. I've never seen any— I've never experienced any of that. I don't want to have to experience that and make those kinds of calls. you know I'dve freaked out. I'dve have like seen this much ice and thought oh my gosh we were going to crash.

turns.speaker: Approach controller (radio)
turns.text: Colgan thirty four oh seven descend and maintain two thousand three hundred.

turns.speaker: First Officer (radio)
turns.text: okay down to two thousand three hundred Colgan thirty four zero seven.

turns.speaker: First Officer (cockpit)
turns.text: I've got you in pitch pitch hold. I don't know if that's what you want.

turns.speaker: Captain (cockpit)
turns.text: yeah that's alright. let's uh— we'll do vertical speed back.

turns.speaker: First Officer (cockpit)
turns.text: but I'm glad to have seen oh— you know now I'm so much more comfortable with it all.

turns.text: yeah uh I I spent the first three months in uh Charleston West Virginia and uh flew—.

documented_events.what_happened: Non-pertinent conversation during descent (sterile-cockpit violation) about the first officer's lack of icing experience; the NTSB lists the failure to adhere to sterile cockpit procedures as a contributing factor.
documented_events.evidence_quote: The pilots were involved in nonpertinent conversation during all phases of flight, including those that are defined as critical by the sterile cockpit rule. For example, the pilots’ nonpertinent conversation during the final minutes of the descent (which included a discussion of their previous experiences flying in icing c onditions) distracted them from their operational tasks.

documented_events.what_happened: First officer flags the autopilot mode to the captain in hedged form; NTSB notes neither pilot corrected the other's procedural deviations.
documented_events.evidence_quote: The NTSB is concerned that, during the accident flight, neither pilot seemed hesitant to engage in nonpertinent conversation or demonstrated correcting behavior when the other pilot deviated from sterile cockpit procedures. These facts suggest that nonpertinent conversation among company pilots during critical phases of flight was not unusual.

notes: Honest limits: this is a hedge of a different kind (deferential, low-assertiveness phrasing 'I don't know if that's what you want'), not the stall-phase failure. The second event's quote is about sterile cockpit deference in general; NTSB does not specifically analyse the 'pitch hold' line. Consider it a weak-to-moderate test.
